reading.body:
The Independent Community Bankers of America filed eight Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI, making it one of the more active banking trade groups on the issue in this dataset.

The filings name twenty lobbyists, and the distribution is uneven. Eleven are named on all eight reports, three on six, three on four, three on two, and one on a single report. That pattern suggests a core team carrying the AI portfolio continuously, with others brought in for specific filings rather than a rotating cast.

Two bills are named in the 2025-or-later filings, HR 2152 and S 2296. The data does not record what the ICBA argued, only that it lobbied. A firm that files for a client reports that it lobbied on an issue, not the position it took.

What this does not tell you is the substance. There is no spending figure, no agency targeted, no text of the bills, and no indication of whether the AI lobbying concerned model regulation, fraud rules, or something else entirely. The count of eight filings is a measure of attention, not of influence.

summary: INDEPENDENT COMMUNITY BANKERS OF AMERICA filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 19194.
